project_skeleton.description: Top-level project skeleton definition. Specifies the runtime language, framework, and module layout that all scaffold entries must be consistent with. This object anchors the technology choices for the entire scaffold artifact. Example 1 (Python/FastAPI): {"language": "python", "framework": "fastapi", "modules": ["src/api/handlers", "src/services", "src/models", "src/core", "tests/unit", "tests/integration"]}. Example 2 (Node/TypeScript + Express): {"language": "typescript", "framework": "express", "modules": ["src/routes", "src/controllers", "src/services", "src/db", "tests/unit", "tests/e2e"]}. Decision rule: `modules` should list directory paths (not file names) that represent the project's logical layer separation. Anti-pattern: listing file names instead of directory paths (e.g., 'auth_handler.py' instead of 'src/auth/') — file names belong in interface_map entries, not in the skeleton; omitting a 'tests/' entry means there is no declared test strategy for the scaffold.

language.description: Primary programming language for this scaffold. Use lowercase with no version suffix. Decision rule: choose the single language that owns the runtime entry point for this scaffold unit — if the project is polyglot, create one scaffold per language boundary. Examples: 'python' for FastAPI or Django services, 'typescript' for Next.js or Express applications, 'go' for high-throughput microservices, 'java' for Spring Boot services, 'rust' for systems or WASM targets. Anti-pattern: 'Python 3.11' (include the version in tech_stack, not here — language is a stable identifier); 'Python/TypeScript' (one language per scaffold — split polyglot projects into separate scaffold entries).

framework.description: Web framework or runtime that drives the scaffold's file structure and conventions. Use lowercase kebab-case. Decision rule: use the framework's canonical package name as it appears in the package registry (PyPI, npm, pkg.go.dev). Examples: 'fastapi' (Python async API service), 'express' (Node.js HTTP server), 'next' (React fullstack with SSR), 'gin' (Go HTTP framework), 'spring-boot' (Java microservice). Omit if the project has no framework (e.g., a pure CLI tool or library). Anti-pattern: 'REST API' (describes the architectural pattern, not the framework — omit or use the actual framework name); 'Django REST Framework' (use kebab-case package name: 'django-rest-framework').

modules.description: Ordered list of top-level modules or packages in this project, following the language/framework's import or package conventions. Examples for Python/FastAPI: ['api', 'models', 'services', 'core', 'tests']. Examples for Go: ['cmd', 'internal', 'pkg', 'api']. Examples for Node.js/TypeScript: ['src/routes', 'src/services', 'src/models', 'src/middleware']. Each entry should correspond to a real directory in the generated scaffold. Anti-pattern: arbitrary names like ['module1', 'module2'] or framework-agnostic names that don't match the ecosystem's conventions.

interface_map.description: Optional. File entries to be scaffolded or generated by this spec. When present, each entry represents a file that must exist in the implementation. Together, these files should constitute a complete, runnable skeleton that satisfies the spec's FRs. Include: source files, test files, configuration files, and any required infrastructure-as-code. Example 1 (Python handler): {"interface_ref": "api-user-authenticate", "path": "src/api/handlers/auth_handler.py", "method": "POST"}. Example 2 (TypeScript route): {"interface_ref": "api-order-create", "path": "src/routes/orders.ts", "method": "POST"}. Decision rule: `path` must be relative from the project root using forward slashes; `method` must match the HTTP method in the corresponding Step 05 API contract; `interface_ref` must match an `api_id` in spec/05_interface_contracts.json. Each interface_ref must appear exactly once across all entries — no two interface_map entries may reference the same interface_ref. Anti-pattern: using absolute paths; mapping both `GET /users/{id}` and `GET /orders/{id}/user` to the same interface_ref when they have different response schemas — each distinct endpoint must have its own interface_ref.

interface_ref.description: Reference to the interface contract (API or component) this scaffold file implements. Should match an api_id or component_id defined in Step 05 (Interface Contracts) or Step 02 (System Sketch) (validated by traceability checks). No two scaffold files may share the same interface_ref — each interface is implemented exactly once (uniqueness enforced by linter).

path.description: Relative file path from the project root. Use forward slashes. Example: 'src/api/handlers/auth_handler.go', 'tests/integration/test_auth.py'. Should not collide with existing files unless replacement is intentional.

method.description: HTTP method for this scaffold endpoint. Must be one of: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS, HEAD. Use the semantically correct method: GET for reads, POST for creates/actions, PUT for full updates, PATCH for partial updates, DELETE for removal.

items.description: An API interface mapping binding an interface reference to an HTTP method and path. Each entry should correspond to a distinct, independently deployable route in the implementation skeleton.

validators.description: Validation checks that have been run against the scaffold to confirm correctness. Each entry is a validator identifier (e.g., 'compile-check', 'lint-pass', 'unit-tests-green'). When build_status is 'green', at least one validator must be present.

command_ref.description: Canonical reference to the CLI command used to generate or validate this scaffold. Kind is structurally pinned to 'command'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:command:pytest", "kind": "command"}. Reference the specific specdev or build command that produces this scaffold. Validated by canonical-integrity lint.

build_status.description: Current build status of the scaffold. Use 'pending' when the scaffold has not yet been built or validated; 'green' when all validators pass and the skeleton compiles/runs; 'red' when at least one validator or build step is failing. A 'green' status requires at least one entry in validators.

trace.description: Traceability links connecting this scaffold to the FRs and APIs it implements. Every scaffold interface mapping must trace to the FR or API it implements. Use type='implements' pointing to fr-* or api-* IDs. Example: [{"type": "implements", "id": "api-user-authenticate", "note": "Scaffold generates the handler file for this API endpoint"}]. Scaffold entries without trace links cannot be validated against the spec step that defined the interface. Consult the items description for approved types and format.

items.description: A single traceability reference. At step 15, use type 'implements' pointing to fr-* IDs (Step 04 FRs the scaffold provides file structure for) or api-* IDs (Step 05 APIs the scaffold generates route handlers for). Example: {"type": "implements", "id": "fr-user-login", "note": "Scaffold generates the authentication route handler and test fixture for this FR"}. Anti-pattern: type 'derives_from' — the scaffold implements requirements, not derives from them.

links.description: External links to related scaffold resources, CI pipelines, or documentation. Use for referencing build dashboards, generated API docs, or deployment guides.

items.description: An external link related to this scaffold (e.g., CI pipeline URL, generated docs, deployment runbook).

allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).
